body: Not sure this needs to be a TODO since it depends on the language support and not on us. Wdyt?
This has a maintenance cost and it'll be hard to detect if we miss to update this test when we introduce a new widget.
These automated tests are hard to read, to maintain and they quickly become conditional. We already cover most of those in each `{widget}-test.ts` files. Why changing the strategy for `$$widgetType`?
if we miss to update this, the test will fail

it's true, but some things should be true for all widgets regardless of what the name is. I found that this gave me more confidence that it is implemented correctly, for example that no typo happened between the test & implementation (which would likely also exist in the test, if it's written manually)

what I meant is that this utility can't be in typedObject, since our polyfill test will fail if source files use object.entries, which is why I put the utility only in the test. I can remove the comment if you don't think it's important
Then you might change the comment from "TODO" to "It's not in the source but in this test because .."

Whenever we adds a widget, we should check this, but might forget to do so (which will be caught by tests). I think it's acceptable to do this test for all widgets in this one place in the uniformed way.
What if we clean up the types for widgets without a connector? Is it a good time to do so? No strong opinion, but genuinely asking.
